title: Volcan: hear your code review instead of scrubbing a diff
status: Plan for the re-take on the live build, not recorded. Every window and timestamp below is an ESTIMATE until video/generate-narration.py measures the narration and a rehearsal measures the product's turns. video/SHOT_LIST.md is the plan in full.
previous_take_script: The 2026-09-29 render of 09d4862 used the six-beat script at commit fc10e7d: git show fc10e7d:video/narration.json
timing_basis: ESTIMATE: each beat's narration at 2.2 words a second of speech_text, the slowest rate of the 2026-09-29 take's beats rounded down, plus the generator's 0.65 s tail and the beat's product window. The cold open fills the title slot.

narration_audio.note: Not generated for this plan. video/generate-narration.py --write-timestamps replaces every timestamp here with measured values.

cold_open.basis: ESTIMATE, not measured. On 2026-09-28 the Findings turn on octocat/Hello-World pull request 1, which has no finding, took 7.47 s and 7.46 s from the click to the browser's speech end event (the product_sound_basis of beat 3 in the previous script). A finding is a longer sentence than No security finding in this change. Replace with the slowest of three rehearsal runs plus 1 s, and write the same figure into cards.title_seconds.
cold_open.visual_action: No title card. The chosen pull request was opened on the live page before the camera rolled, because opening one runs the default engine, an Amazon Bedrock call, and one live digest took 19.67 s on 2026-10-01; the band says so. The first frame is the dialogue under Talk through a real pull request, showing the opened overview, with the next steps outlined. Within the first 0.5 s press Findings when the rehearsal showed at least one finding, otherwise File by file (or the same command typed with Alt and 4 or said with Alt and 5). The page plays its cue and speaks its readback, Understood: findings. or Understood: file by file., then its answer: each finding, file and line as the server words it, or each file with its additions and deletions. These turns read the report already built and call no model. The narrator is silent. The product's own sound and voice are in the mix for the whole turn.
cold_open.gate: The first product sound by 2.0 s and the first spoken word by 5.0 s from the first frame, and the turn plays to its end with nothing over it. A take that misses either is recorded again.

cards.title_slot: cold_open: the title slot carries the cold-open footage, not a text card; the title lines sit in the caption band under it.
title_lines: Volcan on its live build, commit {sha7}. Pull request opened before this shot.
Simulated Alexa+ front end. GitHub review: dry run.
outro_lines: Volcan: code review by ear, by touch and by voice.
Recorded on the live build at commit {sha7}. Simulated Alexa+ front end, not an Alexa skill. GitHub review: a dry run, recorded and not sent.
Narration: synthetic ElevenLabs voice. Product voice: the page's own speech.

beats.narration_text: That was Volcan, live, answering in its own voice. It is a Model Context Protocol server built to be called by Alexa+, so a blind or low-vision developer can review an AI agent's pull request by voice, and hear the verdict first.
beats.speech_text: That was Volcan, live, answering in its own voice. It is a Model Context Protocol server built to be called by Alexa plus, so a blind or low-vision developer can review an A I agent's pull request by voice, and hear the verdict first.
beats.visual_action: The cold-open turn has ended. The view scrolls to the top of the live page: the heading Hear your code review instead of scrubbing a diff, For blind and low-vision developers, the silent preview of the Inverted admin check patch, and the label Live MCP server, simulated Alexa+ front end. Not an Alexa skill. GitHub: dry-run. That label stays on screen; the narration does not open with it. On the last sentence Alt and 1 puts the focus ring on Hear this code review. No product turn in this beat.

beats.narration_text: This patch, an inverted admin check, goes to Claude on Amazon Bedrock. Volcan runs on AWS Lambda, with its review state in Amazon DynamoDB.
beats.speech_text: This patch, an inverted admin check, goes to Claude on Amazon Bedrock. Volcan runs on A W S Lambda, with its review state in Amazon Dynamo D B.
beats.product_sound_basis: ESTIMATE, not measured on this build. One live Bedrock digest of the auth-bypass patch took 19.67 s on 2026-10-01 (docs/EVIDENCE.md, The public deployment). The press comes at the start of this beat, so the narration covers most of that wait; what is left, plus the earcon and the spoken answer (16.74 s of speech for the local engine's sentence on 2026-09-28), is this window. Replace it with the slowest of three rehearsal presses, from the end of the narration to the browser's speech end event, plus 1 s. The narration must end at least 1 s before the fastest rehearsal answer arrives.
beats.visual_action: Enter on Hear this code review at the first frame of the beat, before the narrator speaks: the model call starts and the narrator talks over the wait. The silent preview stays drawn and the button shows it is working. No cut and no speed-up: the wait is shown as it happened. When the answer arrives, after the narrator has stopped, the page plays the falling earcon the server returned and speaks the server's sentence, finding first, while the words light. The product's own sound and voice are in the mix. The engine meter must read Amazon Bedrock; a take whose meter reads local heuristic, or that shows a fallback reason, is recorded again.

beats.narration_text: The meter names Amazon Bedrock, this line says how much of the patch the model read, and this panel opens its full answer.
beats.speech_text: The meter names Amazon Bedrock, this line says how much of the patch the model read, and this panel opens its full answer.
beats.visual_action: Hold on the engine meter reading Amazon Bedrock and the round trip the page measured. Then the coverage line under the spoken caption, exactly as the page prints it: for this short patch, The model read the whole N-character patch., with N as printed. Then open the details The model's full answer and hold on the model's own words. Nothing is typed over the page; every number on screen is one the page printed.

beats.narration_text: Back on the pull request, request changes stages a review, bound to the head commit Volcan read. Listen.
beats.speech_text: Back on the pull request, request changes stages a review, bound to the head commit Volcan read. Listen.

Replace with the slowest of three rehearsal runs on the chosen pull request, from the command to the browser's speech end event for the readback and answer, plus 1 s.
beats.visual_action: Back to Talk through a real pull request, where the chosen pull request is still open. A comment that says it is a dry-run demo goes into the comment box, and Request changes after the narrator stops (or the command request changes followed by that comment, typed with Alt and 4). The page plays its cue and speaks its readback, then Ready to request changes on the pull request, bound to head commit and its first seven characters, with the comment, then Say confirm to submit it, or cancel. State AWAITING CONFIRM, with Confirm and Cancel outlined. The whole turn is in the mix as the product's voice; nothing talks over it.

beats.narration_text: Nothing leaves until you confirm, and this build has no GitHub token, so it records the review and sends nothing. Confirm, and listen.
beats.speech_text: Nothing leaves until you confirm, and this build has no GitHub token, so it records the review and sends nothing. Confirm, and listen.
beats.product_sound_basis: Measured on 2026-09-28 against a local server on port 8871, each time after Request changes on octocat/Hello-World pull request 1: 22.1 s and 21.8 s in two rehearsals and 21.96 s in a full rehearsal take, from the click on Confirm to the browser's speech end event for its readback and answer. Re-measure on the live build with the chosen pull request.
beats.visual_action: Confirm after the narrator stops. The page plays its cue and speaks Understood: confirm., then Dry run. Nothing was sent to GitHub. The head commit is still the commit it read, and the exact request Volcan would send has been recorded. A live send would be refused: no GITHUB_TOKEN is set. State RECORDED, NOT SENT. Midway the view moves to the review pane: outcome recorded and not sent, the live head re-read, and the exact POST request body the server recorded.

beats.narration_text: This handshake is a real one with the server under the page, at protocol revision 2025-11-25. Alexa+ itself has never called Volcan.
beats.speech_text: This handshake is a real one with the server under the page, at protocol revision twenty twenty-five, eleven, twenty-five. Alexa plus itself has never called Volcan.
beats.visual_action: Evidence, tab Server and MCP: Server reached, with the commit and the model path the live server reports. On the first sentence press Run a real MCP handshake, which sends initialize and tools/list and calls no tool, and hold on the negotiated version 2025-11-25 and the tool list as the page prints them. On the last sentence the connection strip and its Alexa+ box, which reads package built and tested locally, not certified or deployed. Then the closing card. Do not press Replay the documented Alexa+ requests on the live build: each of its three clients calls digest_semantic_diff with the default engine, so one press is three billed Bedrock calls and could run close to a minute.
